sections.title: Even ours

fields.label: Summary
fields.text: Owners rarely choose to stay with their energy supplier. The notice date passes during service, and the contract runs on. A business contract has none of the protection a household has: it renews as written. SGB's advisors call before every notice date, SGB's own contracts included. We make that the whole campaign: an energy supplier that tells you when you can leave it. It answers the owner's distrust of energy calls with the one call that works for the owner, and it shows the personal advisor at work instead of claiming one.

fields.label: How we bring your idea to life, in one sentence
fields.text: Every piece shows the notice date that slips by in service, and the SGB advisor who calls before it, even on SGB's own contracts.

head: Question
What we found
Source
rows: Do business contracts renew when the owner misses the notice date?

Yes. Since March 2022 a household's energy contract may only roll on month by month after its first term. That rule protects consumers only. A business gets what its contract says, and a common clause renews it by 12 months with three months' notice. SGB's own Portfolio tariff renews by 12 months without notice.
energiehelden24.nrw, Gewerbestrom und Gewerbegas kündigen (read 10 Nov 2026); Verbraucherzentrale Niedersachsen; SGB news post (ref 1.3)
Do owners miss it?

Partly supported. A broker writes that many businesses assume the household rule applies to them and then find another year added. We found no survey with a share. We list it as an assumption and propose that SGB's advisors count, in week 1 to 4, how many new leads had a contract that renewed without a choice: [share of leads with an unchosen renewal].
energiehelden24.nrw (a broker's statement, not research); assumption
Is there a second date owners miss?

Yes. When a supplier raises prices, a business may cancel without notice, but the supplier only has to tell a business two weeks ahead (a household: one month). A letter opened late closes that window too.
energiehelden24.nrw, Sonderkündigung (read 10 Nov 2026); to be confirmed by SGB
Why do owners hang up on energy calls?

Energy contracts are among the products most sold by cold call in Germany. The Federal Network Agency can only fine cold calls to consumers; calls to businesses are not fined. So an owner hears from energy companies mostly when a stranger calls.
Bundesnetzagentur, Unerlaubte Telefonwerbung (read 10 Nov 2026)
Could another supplier sign the idea?

A reminder alone, no: brokers already offer to note contract ends and remind. The twist is what nobody else can say. A broker is not the supplier, and a supplier does not remind you to leave it. Every piece keeps the twist.
energiehelden24.nrw offers reminders; swap test

sections.title: Meet your supplier

fields.label: Summary
fields.text: A restaurant runs on suppliers the owner knows by name. The butcher, the brewery's driver and the wine merchant come to the door. Energy is one of the biggest bills on the desk, and it has no face: the energy people who call are strangers, and owners hang up. SGB is the exception. Its advisors visit on site and stay the one contact person. We introduce SGB the way every good supplier is introduced in hospitality: in person, at the door, by name.

fields.label: Our insight, in one sentence
fields.text: Owners trust the suppliers they have met, and energy is the one big supplier they never meet.

fields.label: Our idea, in one sentence
fields.text: SGB is the energy supplier that comes to the door like every other supplier, so owners meet their advisor before they hear a sales pitch.

The energy voice an owner knows is a stranger's voice on the phone.

Restaurants and hotels felt energy hardest: in a DEHOGA survey of 3,850 businesses (September 2022), energy costs rose 55% on average from October 2022 and 96% from January 2023. 48.8% of businesses then put energy at 10% of turnover or more.

head: Item
Our proposal
rows: What runs

Weeks 1–2: both tracks, cells A to F, on Meta (Facebook and Instagram, 4:5 and 9:16) and LinkedIn (4:5), one audience: owners and managers of restaurants and hotels in Germany. Search runs on its own budget line, Track B promise.
Budget split
Tracks 50/50. Within a track: A 20%, B 15%, C 20%, D 15%, E 15%, F 15%. Meta 70%, LinkedIn 30%. Search outside the split. Same daily caps for both tracks.
Main metric
Cost per qualified lead for A to E. Cost per signed contract for F.
Lead status feedback

The advisor marks each lead qualified or not within two working days in SGB's CRM. The status goes back daily as an offline conversion: Meta Conversions API, LinkedIn Conversions API, Google offline conversion import. Bidding learns from qualified leads, not from forms.
Decision rule

Week 3: stop a cell when its cost per qualified lead is more than 1.5 times the track's median after at least [minimum leads per cell] leads. Never stop on clicks. Week 4: move the stopped budget to the best two cells of each track; compare tracks on cost per qualified lead at equal spend.
Weekly report

Per track and cell: spend, impressions, clicks, page visits, form starts, leads, qualified leads, cost per qualified lead, signed contracts (F), quiz starts and completions (D), and the share of leads with an unchosen renewal.

items: [callback time]: SGB's callback time for a lead.
[advisor name], [region]: a real advisor who agrees to appear, with written consent.
[weeks before]: how long before a notice date the advisor calls.
[share of leads with an unchosen renewal]: to be counted by advisors from week 1.
[band 1] to [band 4]: monthly bill bands that split SLP from RLM; SGB sets them.
[minimum leads per cell]: the smallest count before a stop decision; set with SGB's media budget.
The quiz fits (more fixed, more spot, a mix) are proposed; SGB has not confirmed them.
Owners distrust energy calls: brief hypothesis, not yet tested.
The two-week notice for price changes to businesses: from a broker's guide, to be confirmed by SGB.

All photography is shot for SGB with real owners and advisors, with written consent.
